title: The talents — his own servants, his goods delivered, the reckoning at his coming, and the one cast out (Luke 19; Daniel 7; Proverbs 13; Revelation 2)
summary:
It ain't new. A lord who goes away, leaves his goods with his own servants, and comes back to reckon with them: the prophets had the saints taking the kingdom, and the proverbs had the sluggard with nothing, long before Matthew wrote the parable down:

*For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.* (Matthew 25:14)

*And unto one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to every man according to his several ability; and straightway took his journey.* (Matthew 25:15)

Mark who they are. Not strangers, not hired men off the road, but his own servants, each given a share of what is his. Luke tells it with pounds and a nobleman gone to receive a kingdom:

*He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.* (Luke 19:12)

*And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.* (Luke 19:13)

Mark has the same house and the same journey, with the charge to watch:

*For the Son of Adam is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch.* (Mark 13:34)

Then the lord comes back:

*After a long time the lord of those servants cometh, and reckoneth with them.* (Matthew 25:19)

*His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.* (Matthew 25:21)

*Then he which had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou hast not strawed:* (Matthew 25:24)

*And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth: lo, there thou hast that is thine.* (Matthew 25:25)

*His lord answered and said unto him, Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I sowed not, and gather where I have not strawed:* (Matthew 25:26)

*And cast ye the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.* (Matthew 25:30)

The one cast out was given a talent, called a servant, and reckoned with as one of the household. He is not a tare and not one of the nations. He is of the house, and he is judged by what he did with what he was given. Luke says the same of the servant who knew his lord's will:

*And that servant, which knew his lord’s will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.* (Luke 12:47)

And Matthew had already said who it is that ends in outer darkness:

*But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.* (Matthew 8:12)

The proverbs had the slothful man's end long before:

*The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing: but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.* (Proverbs 13:4)

*Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:* (Proverbs 6:6)

What the faithful are given is rule, and Daniel had seen whose that rule is:

*But the saints of the El Elyon (most High) shall take the kingdom, and possess the kingdom for ever, even for ever and ever.* (Daniel 7:18)

*And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the El Elyon (most High), whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.* (Daniel 7:27)

The twelve thrones and the reign on the earth are that same rule, promised to the same servants, and the one who gets it is the one who keeps his works to the end:

*And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28)

*And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations:* (Revelation 2:26)

*And hast made us unto our Elohim (God) kings and priests: and we shall reign on the earth.* (Revelation 5:10)

The talents are the gifts, dealt to each by measure, and Peter says what a servant does with a gift:

*As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of Elohim (God).* (1 Peter 4:10)

*For unto every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but from him that hath not shall be taken away even that which he hath.* (Matthew 25:29)

The reckoning is of the house, by works, at his coming. The one with his talent in the ground was no stranger, and the door he is put out of was his own lord's. So the parable ends where the chapter before it did:

*Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.* (Matthew 24:42)

2975.prose: Luke says why Yahusha (Jesus) told it: they thought the kingdom *should immediately appear*. So he tells of a man who goes away first and comes back later, and the servants he leaves behind have work to do in between. The kingdom is not on the doorstep today.
2975.phrase: they thought that the kingdom of Elohim (God) should immediately appear
2975.sentence: The crowd expected the kingdom at once, so the parable sets a going away and a coming back between them and it.

2976.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says this about the parables, and it is the rule the goods run by. The one who uses what he has is given *more abundance*. The one who has nothing to show loses *even that he hath*. The servant handed his master's goods is under this rule from the start.
2976.phrase: whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath
2976.sentence: What a servant is handed is increased if he uses it and taken back if he does not.

2977.prose: Just before the parable Yahusha (Jesus) asks who the faithful and wise servant is, the one set over the household. Same household, same servants. The man who goes away leaves his goods with servants of that kind, and the one who is found doing the work is the one he rewards.
2977.phrase: ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season
2977.sentence: The servant set over the household is the kind of servant the goods are left with.

2978.prose: Faithful servants are handed rule, and Yahusha (Jesus) says what it is: *power over the nations* for the one who *keepeth my works unto the end*. The servant in the parable is told to keep what is put in his hands, and this is the other side of it. The reward is rule.
2978.phrase: keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations
2978.sentence: Keeping his works to the end is what earns the servant power over the nations.

2979.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) overcame and sits with his Father in his throne. The servant who overcomes is promised a place beside him: *sit with me in my throne*. The goods the master leaves with his own servants lead to a seat, and the seat is his own.
2979.phrase: to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame
2979.sentence: The overcoming servant is given a seat in the throne of the one who overcame first.

2980.prose: The goods handed over in the far country come back as rule. Those made *kings and priests* to their Elohim (God) *shall reign on the earth*. The servants are his own, and the reign is theirs to hold under him, and it is on the earth, not somewhere else.
2980.phrase: hast made us unto our Elohim (God) kings and priests: and we shall reign on the earth
2980.sentence: The servants end as kings and priests who reign on the earth.

2981.prose: Peter asks what those who followed will get. Yahusha (Jesus) answers with *twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes* of Yashar'el (Israel). That is the rule the faithful servant is brought into, and it is rule over the house, when the Son of Adam sits on the throne of his glory.
2981.phrase: ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)
2981.sentence: The servants who followed him sit on twelve thrones over the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).

2982.prose: Daniel was told what the parable ends on: the saints *shall take the kingdom*. The servants given the goods are the ones who end up holding it, and it is for good, *for ever and ever*. The prophet had it long before Matthew wrote the story down.
2982.phrase: saints of the El Elyon (most High) shall take the kingdom, and possess the kingdom for ever
2982.sentence: The saints receive the kingdom and keep it for ever, which is what the faithful servants are brought into.

2983.prose: Judgment comes first. *Until the Ancient of days came*, the saints did not hold the kingdom; then *judgment was given to the saints* and they possessed it. The coming and the reckoning arrive together here, as they do when the master returns to settle with his servants.
2983.phrase: judgment was given to the saints of the El Elyon (most High); and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom
2983.sentence: When the Ancient of days comes, judgment is given to the saints and they possess the kingdom.

2984.prose: The kingdom is given to *the people of the saints*, and it is *an everlasting kingdom*. The talents were a small thing beside what Daniel saw handed over, the whole kingdom *under the whole heaven*. The servants who held what was given them are the ones it is given to.
2984.phrase: shall be given to the people of the saints of the El Elyon (most High), whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom
2984.sentence: The whole kingdom is given to the people of the saints, and it does not end.

2985.prose: A sluggard is told to *go to the ant* and *consider her ways, and be wise*. The servant who hid his talent in the earth is the one who needed that word. He was given a share and did nothing with it. The old writings already had the lazy servant's picture.
2985.phrase: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise
2985.sentence: The sluggard is sent to the ant to learn, and the servant with the buried talent is the one sent.

2986.prose: The sluggard *desireth, and hath nothing*, and that is where the servant with the buried talent ends, with even that taken from him. The diligent *shall be made fat*, which is the other servants, handed more. The proverb had the pair long before the parable.
2986.sentence: The sluggard ends with nothing and the diligent are made fat, the two ends of the servants.

2987.prose: Gifts differ, and the giver is the same. The servants are handed his goods in different measures, and every share comes out of the same stock. Paul puts it as *diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit*. What a servant holds is his master's, whatever the size.
2987.phrase: there are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit
2987.sentence: The gifts differ in kind and size, but they all come from one giver.

2988.prose: Paul says Elohim (God) has *dealt to every man the measure*, and no one is to think more of himself than he ought. The servants in the parable each get a share of the goods by measure, and each is answerable for his own share. Nobody is handed everything and nobody is handed nothing.
2988.phrase: according as Elohim (God) hath dealt to every man the measure of faith
2988.sentence: Each man is dealt a measure, and thinking soberly means owning what he was dealt and no more.

2989.prose: Peter puts the parable in one line. The gift is received, and the servant is a steward of it, to *minister the same one to another*. The goods were never his own, and a good steward uses them for the household instead of burying them.
2989.phrase: minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of Elohim (God)
2989.sentence: A servant who has received a gift is to spend it on others as a good steward.

7080.prose: A ruler asks what he must do to inherit. Matthew's parable gives the shape of the answer: a man leaves *his goods* with *his own servants*, and each is held to what he did with them. Doing is the stewarding of what is put in your hands, and it is reckoned when the master comes.
7080.phrase: travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods
7080.sentence: The goods left with his own servants are what the ruler's question about doing comes down to.

5298.prose: Mark leaves the porter told *to watch*. Matthew puts the same charge in the mouth of Yahusha (Jesus): *Watch therefore*, for the hour is not known. The servants left with their work are the ones watching for the one who left them.
5298.phrase: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come
5298.sentence: The watch the porter is told to keep is a watch for an hour no one knows.

7090.prose: Luke has them thinking the kingdom would *appear* at once. Matthew gives the same kind of story without the nobleman and says plainly what the kingdom is like: a man goes away and leaves *his goods* with *his own servants*. The kingdom is not arriving today. There is a going, and servants given work in between.
7090.phrase: travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods
7090.sentence: The kingdom is a man who goes away and leaves his goods with his own servants, not something appearing at once.

5299.prose: Mark has a man *taking a far journey* who gives *authority to his servants*. Matthew has the same man, *travelling into a far country*, calling *his own servants* and handing over *his goods*. What Mark calls authority and work, Matthew calls goods put in their hands. The servants are his in both.
5299.phrase: a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants
5299.sentence: The same man goes on the same journey and leaves his own servants with what is his.

5300.prose: Mark leaves the porter told to watch. Luke says how it is done: loins *girded about* and *lights burning*. A servant who is ready is dressed and has the lamp lit, so that when his master comes he is not caught asleep.
5300.phrase: Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning
5300.sentence: Watching means being dressed for work with the light on, ready for the master's return.

fable_read: Claude Fable 5.1 read every card: 2980 Revelation 5:10 read through Daniel 7 ('the same rule Daniel saw') removed — Revelation in its own words; 2983 'held down' made plain.
